recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If FM wants billablePeriod or serviced[x] removed, open or apply a new explicit tracker because that would require coordinated structure, example, model-definition, and migration updates beyond this issue's demonstrated application.
issue_request: FHIR-31062 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. It requested a reusable Dates backbone across Claim, ClaimResponse, CoverageEligibilityRequest, CoverageEligibilityResponse, and ExplanationOfBenefit, with type 1..1 CodeableConcept and when 1..1 date-or-Period, and originally suggested replacing CoverageEligibility serviced[x] and Claim/EOB billablePeriod. The final resolution required a 0..* dates-style backbone, left the actual element name to be determined, and said the element would not be used for line-item service dates or periods.
initial_application: The issue was applied by commit 7b44f67dcefe7f6602e4969c296818527ae3567c and merged by a04d004d1fb5de1905898d001d3301dd1d6bd682. That implementation added event backbones to all five listed resources and added the datestype code system/value set. Current source still contains those elements and terminology.
additional_context: The relevant resources are active in source/fhir.ini. Current source also retains Claim.billablePeriod, ExplanationOfBenefit.billablePeriod, and CoverageEligibilityRequest/Response.serviced[x]; because the explicit FHIR-31062 implementation was later Published and the final resolution was modified, those retained specific elements were treated as part of the accepted application rather than a missing fix. Later Applied FHIR-53057 changed CoverageEligibilityResponse.event.type binding to preferred. Triaged FHIR-50910 proposes moving datestype to THO and changing the binding, but is not a final source-edit decision in this default run. No relevant conflicting Zulip or Confluence evidence was found.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The published empty commit records that current source already implements the requested backbone under the final chosen name event, with event.type CodeableConcept and event.when[x] dateTime-or-Period in each requested resource. Removing older specific date fields now would be a broader breaking change unsupported by discovered final evidence.
